methodology_other: Dataset generated using deep learning algorithms to classify road surfaces.
name: angola-road-surface-data
notes:
This dataset provides detailed information on road surfaces from OpenStreetMap (OSM),
distinguishing between **paved** and **unpaved** roads across the region.

Surface classification is derived using a hybrid deep learning approach.
For methodological details, see:
http://arxiv.org/abs/2410.19874

Recently, we also published a new country-level dataset based on PlanetScope satellite imagery
with near-complete coverage of all arterial roads. It is available on HDX under the name
Angola **Planet** Road Surface.
The corresponding paper is available at:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04092


Road Surface Statistics

Approximately 0.284 million km of roads are mapped in OSM in this region.

Based on AI-derived estimates:
- Paved roads: 0.024 million km (8.4616%)
- Unpaved roads: 0.1105 million km (38.9039%)

About 0.1495 million km
(52.6345%) of road surface information is missing in OSM.

To reduce this gap, the Mapillary-derived road surface dataset provides an additional
0.0002 million km
(0.15%) of the missing surface information.


Intended Use

This dataset supports transportation planning, infrastructure analysis,
climate emissions assessment, and GIS applications.


AI Features

- **pred_class**: Model-predicted surface class ("paved" or "unpaved")
- **pred_label**: Binary label (0 = paved, 1 = unpaved)
- **osm_surface_class**: Surface classification derived from OSM tags
- **combined_surface_osm_priority**: Combined classification prioritizing OSM
- **combined_surface_DL_priority**: Combined classification prioritizing DL prediction
- **n_of_predictions_used**: Number of predictions used for estimation
- **predicted_length**: Predicted length based on DL estimation (meters)
- **DL_mean_timestamp**: Mean timestamp of predictions used


OSM Attributes

- **name**
- **name:en**
- **name:* (local language)**
- **highway**
- **surface**
- **smoothness**
- **width**
- **lanes**
- **oneway**
- **bridge**
- **layer**
- **source**


Urban Classification Attributes

- **continent**
- **country_iso_a2**
- **urban** (0 = rural, 1 = urban)
- **urban_area**
- **osm_id**
- **osm_type**


Data Sources

The dataset originates from OpenStreetMap (OSM) and is augmented with
deep learning predictions based on Mapillary street-level imagery,
combined with the GHSU Global Human Settlement Urban Layer 2019
and AFRICAPOLIS 2020 urban layer.

More HeiGIT datasets:
https://data.humdata.org/organization/heidelberg-institute-for-geoinformation-technology

More information:
https://heigit.org/

Contact:
communications@heigit.org

organization.title: HeiGIT (Heidelberg Institute for Geoinformation Technology)
organization.description:
HeiGIT (Heidelberg Institute for Geoinformation Technology) performs applied research relating to geographic information. Results and data are made freely available for the benefit of the environment and society through stakeholders such as researchers and aid organizations & associations.

The core foci of HeiGIT range from supporting humanitarian missions with customized geodata, to developing intelligent routing solutions for disasters or heatwaves. HeiGIT also implements innovative methods from the fields of spatial data processing and machine learning to analyze, enrich, and visualize geodata (e.g. OpenStreetMap data), as well as offering practical data analysis for climate protection initiatives.

HeiGIT gGmbH was founded in 2019 as an affiliated institute of Heidelberg University, with core funding from the Klaus Tschira Foundation.
